key_insight: At high Womersley number and small oscillation amplitude, the hydrodynamic resistance of a floating planar body on an air-water interface is well described by an oscillatory Stokes boundary layer with added-mass and damping effects.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to predict and measure unsteady interfacial drag for oscillating floats, sensors, and actuated devices at fluid interfaces.
method: Magnetically drive planar floating bodies into harmonic lateral oscillation.
Measure steady-state amplitude response and phase lag across frequencies, masses, sizes, and shapes.
Use frequency-response data and startup transients to extract effective added mass, damping, and history effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental frequency-response measurements and startup transients that agree with oscillatory boundary-layer theory and a history-integral model.
watch_item: The theory and extracted coefficients are most reliable in the small-deformation regime, so larger interfacial motions may require a more complete model.
paper_title: Hydrodynamic Resistance on Oscillating Planar Interfacial Bodies
